Let $S$ be a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety. A **geometric
polarizable rational Hodge variation** on $S$ consists of a finite-rank rational
local system $H$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), a
continuous pure Hodge decomposition of its fibers, or a finite direct sum of
pure weights, in the sense of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], and an
algebraic realization on a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq S$: there are
smooth projective morphisms $f_i:X_i\to U$, degrees $m_i$ and integers $r_i$
such that $H|_U$ is a Hodge direct summand of
$$\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i),$$
where $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the Tate structure of
[[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. A **Hodge direct summand** means the
image of a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism at every point.

$W_{-3}=0$, $W_{-2}=W_{-1}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $W_0=H$ and the decreasing
filtration $F^1H_{\mathbb C}=0$, $F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$,
$F^{-1}H_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$, with $i\in\mathbb C$ satisfying
$i^2=-1$ and conjugation $\sigma(z)=\bar z$
([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]).

[F1] A rational mixed Hodge structure is the datum of a finite increasing $W$ and a finite decreasing $F$ such that on every $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtrations are $n$-opposed, i.e. split into the pieces $H^{p,q}_n$ with $\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$; a morphism preserves $W$ and $F$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F2] The Tate structure $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the pure structure of weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type $(-r,-r)$; in particular $\mathbb Q(1)$ has weight $-2$ and type $(-1,-1)$, while $\mathbb Q(0)$ has weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

[F3] On a graded piece $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ the induced filtration $F$ is the image of $F\cap W_n$ and $\bar F=\sigma(F)$; the summands are $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

1.1 The weight filtration is finite with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-1}=0$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0=H/\mathbb Q e_1\cong\mathbb Q e_0$. On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$ the induced $F$ has $F^0=0$ and $F^{-1}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$, since $F^0\cap W_{-2}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)\cap\mathbb C e_1=0$; the conjugate filtration satisfies $\bar F^{-1}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$ and $\bar F^0=0$ for the same reason, so the pieces are $H^{-1,-1}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}$ and nothing else, and $H^{-1,-1}$ is spanned by the image of $e_1$, which is rational. On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$ the image of $F^0\cap W_0=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$ is all of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$ because $e_0+ie_1\mapsto e_0\ne0$, and $F^1=0$; the conjugate $\bar F^0=\sigma(F^0)=\mathbb C(e_0-ie_1)$ likewise has image all of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$, so the pieces are $H^{0,0}=\operatorname{Gr}^W_0$ and nothing else. Both graded pieces are therefore $n$-opposed, with the rational structure of $e_1$ and $e_0$ respectively, so $(H,W,F)$ is a rational mixed Hodge structure; its graded pieces are $\mathbb Q(1)$ and $\mathbb Q(0)$ in the convention [F2]. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Let $\iota\colon\mathbb Q(1)\to H$ be the inclusion $\mathbb C\to H_{\mathbb C}$ sending $1$ to $e_1$ and let $\pi\colon H\to\mathbb Q(0)$ be the $\mathbb Q$-linear map $e_0\mapsto1$, $e_1\mapsto0$. Both preserve the filtrations: $\iota$ sends the weight-$(-2)$ structure into $W_{-2}H=\mathbb Q e_1$ and $F^{-1}\mathbb Q(1)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ into $F^{-1}H_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$, while $F^0\mathbb Q(1)_{\mathbb C}=0$; and $\pi$ satisfies $\pi(W_{-1}H)=0=W_{-1}\mathbb Q(0)$ and $\pi(W_0H)=\mathbb Q(0)=W_0\mathbb Q(0)$, $\pi(F^0H_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\mathbb C=F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C}$ and $\pi(F^1H_{\mathbb C})=0$. Hence $0\to\mathbb Q(1)\xrightarrow{\iota}H\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbb Q(0)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of rational mixed Hodge structures, with $\ker\pi=\mathbb Q e_1$. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Every $\mathbb Q$-linear section $s$ of $\pi$ satisfies $s(1)=e_0+q e_1$ with $q\in\mathbb Q$, because $\pi(e_0+q e_1)=1$ and $\pi(e_1)=0$. If $s$ were a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, it would satisfy $s_{\mathbb C}(F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$; since $F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ and $s_{\mathbb C}(1)=e_0+qe_1$, there would be $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $e_0+qe_1=\lambda(e_0+ie_1)$. Comparing the coefficients of $e_0$ and $e_1$ in the basis $(e_0,e_1)$ gives $\lambda=1$ and $q=i$, which is impossible for $q\in\mathbb Q$. Hence the extension does not split in the category of rational mixed Hodge structures. The obstruction is visible directly in the $(0,0)$-direction: $F^0H_{\mathbb C}\cap\bar F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)\cap\mathbb C(e_0-ie_1)=0$, while a rational section must send $1$ into a rational vector of $F^0$, which is then also fixed by conjugation and hence would have to lie in this zero intersection. [given, F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]); the complexified map is written
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and commutes with the conjugations because
$f$ is rational.

[F1] The Deligne splitting of [[lem-deligne-splitting-of-a-mixed-hodge-structure]]: $H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p,q}I^{p,q}(H)$ with $W_mH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q\le m}I^{p,q}(H)$, $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}(H)$, the projection of $I^{p,q}(H)$ onto $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{p+q}H_{\mathbb C}$ being an isomorphism onto $H^{p,q}_{p+q}$, and $f_{\mathbb C}(I^{p,q}(H))\subseteq I^{p,q}(K)$. The conjugation formula is only $I^{p,q}+W_{p+q-2}=\sigma(I^{q,p})+W_{p+q-2}$; no exact $\bar F$ partial-sum formula by the same pieces is used.

[F2] On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ one has $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n$ with $H^{p,q}_n=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_n\cap\bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

1.1 (Weight strictness.) Let $y=f(x)\in f(H)\cap W_nK$ and decompose $x=\sum_{p,q}x^{p,q}$ along the splitting of $H_{\mathbb C}$; then $y=\sum_{p,q}f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ with $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})\in I^{p,q}(K)$ by [F1]. Since $y\in W_nK=\bigoplus_{p+q\le n}I^{p,q}(K)$ and the sum is direct, all components with $p+q>n$ vanish: $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ whenever $p+q>n$. Hence $x':=\sum_{p+q\le n}x^{p,q}$ lies in $W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ and satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(x')=y$, so $y\in f_{\mathbb C}(W_nH_{\mathbb C})$. The reverse inclusion $f(W_nH)\subseteq f(H)\cap W_nK$ is the preservation of $W$ by $f$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 (Hodge strictness.) The same computation with the condition $p<a$ instead of $p+q>n$: if $y=f_{\mathbb C}(x)\in f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^aK_{\mathbb C}$, decompose $x$ and use $F^aK_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}I^{p,q}(K)$ to conclude that $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ for $p<a$, so $x'=\sum_{p\ge a}x^{p,q}$ lies in $F^aH_{\mathbb C}$ and maps to $y$. [F1, algebra]

2.2 (Exactness of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$.) Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to 0$ be a short exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures. By [F1] the splitting identifies $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nA$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nB$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nC$ with $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}I^{p,q}(A)$ and its analogues, and the maps $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n i$, $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n p$ with the direct sums of the maps induced by $i$ and $p$ between the pieces $I^{p,q}$. Each piecewise sequence $0\to I^{p,q}(A)\to I^{p,q}(B)\to I^{p,q}(C)\to 0$ is exact: the middle arrows are the restrictions of the injective $i$ and of the surjective $p$, and an element $b\in I^{p,q}(B)$ lies in $\ker p$ precisely when $b=i(a)$ for some $a\in A$, and decomposing $a$ into its $I$-pieces shows that all other pieces map to zero; since $i$ is injective, they vanish and $a\in I^{p,q}(A)$. A direct sum of short exact sequences is short exact, so $0\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nA\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nB\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_nC\to0$ is exact; a morphism is strict for $W$ precisely when it induces such exact sequences, so this recovers step 1.1 independently. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Kernel, image and cokernel.) The functorial splitting [F1] makes $f_{\mathbb C}$ a direct sum of maps $I^{p,q}(H)\to I^{p,q}(K)$. Thus its kernel, image and cokernel decompose into the respective kernels, images and cokernels of these maps, and their induced or quotient $W$ and $F$ are the partial sums by $p+q\le n$ and $p\ge a$. The projection isomorphisms in [F1] identify their weight-$n$ pieces, with these induced $F$ filtrations, with the kernel, image and cokernel of $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n f$, computed componentwise in the pure decompositions $H^{p,q}_n,K^{p,q}_n$. These identifications are the canonical rational graded maps: for a kernel this follows from $W$ strictness, since if $f(x)\in W_{n-1}K$ with $x\in W_nH$, choose $y\in W_{n-1}H$ with $f(y)=f(x)$ and replace $x$ by $x-y$; the image and cokernel follow by the same induced/quotient description. The graded rational map commutes with conjugation and preserves $F$, hence also $\bar F$; between equal-weight pure structures it preserves each type $F^p\cap\bar F^q$ with $p+q=n$. Consequently its pure kernels, images and cokernels have conjugation exchanging their $(p,q)$ and $(q,p)$ pieces. Their $F$ partial sums and their conjugates are therefore $n$-opposed. Every weight-graded piece of the three rational filtered spaces satisfies the mixed Hodge axiom, proving the claim. This argument requires no exact conjugate decomposition on the mixed vector space. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

Resolve the complexes and their filtrations by the exact Godement construction: $C^0(A)(V)=\prod_{x\in V}A_x$, with the natural embedding and successive cokernels. Stalks and products are exact for vector spaces under AC. Moreover $C^0(A)=\prod_{x\in X}i_{x*}A_x$ is an injective sheaf of field-vector spaces: each $A_x$ is injective over its field by extension of linear maps along a chosen complement, the exact stalk functor is left adjoint to $i_{x*}$, and a product of injectives is injective because the component extension maps can be chosen simultaneously under AC. Replace the rational and comparison models by $\tau_{\le d}$ first; their cohomology sheaves above $d$ vanish by the local torus calculation, so this is a quasi-isomorphism and leaves a finite weight range $0\le a\le d$.
